summary: Belize is visa-free for US, UK, EU, Canadian, Australian, CARICOM and most Commonwealth passports, with visitors stamped in for up to 30 days and monthly extensions available for a fee. Other nationalities need a consular visa — though holders of a valid multiple-entry US visa are generally exempted.

defaultSource.name: Belize Immigration Department — Do you need a visa to travel to Belize? (country table)

AF.notes: A visa from a Belizean consulate is required before travel. Holders of a valid multiple-entry US, Canadian or Schengen visa, or of a US or Canadian permanent residence card, are exempt for visits of up to 30 days, and some travelers can arrange clearance to pay the visa fee on arrival. Confirm with the Belize Immigration Department.

conditionalWaivers.text: Travelers whose nationality would normally need a Belizean visa are exempt for visits of up to 30 days if they hold a valid multiple-entry US visa or a US permanent residence card. The same exemption covers a valid multiple-entry Schengen visa, and a valid multiple-entry Canadian visa or Canadian permanent residence card. Border officers still decide on entry.

source.name: Belize Immigration Department — Do you need a visa to travel to Belize?

fee.notes: Single-entry visa, valid 6 months: BZD 200 for most nationalities, BZD 750 for nationals of India, Nepal, Thailand, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Pakistan and Sri Lanka, and BZD 3,000 for nationals of the People's Republic of China. A multiple-entry visa, valid 12 months, costs BZD 300, 1,000 or 4,000 respectively.
Some visa-required nationalities can pay the visa fee on arrival, but only with clearance arranged in advance through the Immigration Department — do not travel without written approval.
BZD 200 (about USD 100) for each 30-day Visitor's Permit Extension, the same for all nationalities. Apply at an Immigration office before your current stamp expires.

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 3 months beyond your departure date from Belize. Many airlines apply a stricter 6-month rule, so 6 months' validity is the safe choice.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required only for travelers arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. It is not needed on direct arrivals from North America or Europe.

travelInsurance.text: Travel insurance is not required to enter Belize. The Belize Travel Health Insurance that arriving tourists had to buy during the pandemic became optional in July 2022, when Statutory Instrument No. 100 of 2022 replaced the COVID-19 entry regulations and Cabinet removed all public-health measures at points of entry. Cover for medical emergencies is still sensible.

source.name: Government of Belize Press Office — Cabinet Brief, 14 July 2022 (removal of all public-health measures at points of entry)
source.instrument: Statutory Instrument No. 100 of 2022, Public Health (Reform) (Prevention of the Spread of Infectious Disease) (COVID-19) Regulations, 2022 — in force 12 July 2022, repealing S.I. 61 of 2022; contains no entry or insurance requirement

onwardTicket.text: Immigration officers routinely ask for a return or onward ticket and the address where you will be staying.

proofOfFunds.text: Visitors must be able to show sufficient funds to cover their stay. No official source publishes a per-day amount; the immigration officer judges what is sufficient.

currencyLimits.text: Currency worth USD 10,000 or more (or the equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure.

notes: Taking coral, conch shells, turtle products or other marine life out of Belize without a permit is prohibited.
Firearms and ammunition are strictly prohibited without prior authorization — penalties are severe.

payments.text: The Belize dollar is pegged 2:1 to the US dollar, and US dollars are accepted virtually everywhere. Cards work at hotels, dive shops and larger restaurants (often with a surcharge); carry cash for small vendors on the cayes, taxis and villages.

safety.text: The main tourist areas — the cayes, Placencia, San Ignacio — are generally safe. Belize City has a high rate of gang-related violent crime concentrated on its south side; avoid walking there after dark and use licensed taxis (green plates).

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Belize travel advice

bestTimeToVisit.text: The dry season from December to April is ideal for the cayes, diving and the Maya ruins. Hurricane season runs June to November, with the wettest months from September to November.

tips.text: If your nationality needs a Belizean visa but you hold a valid multiple-entry US visa, you are generally allowed in without one — travel on the passport containing the US visa and confirm with a consulate before flying.
Leaving Belize overland to Guatemala or Mexico costs a border exit fee of about BZD 40 (USD 20) per person, payable in cash. Air departure taxes are normally included in your ticket.
Even visa-free visitors are stamped in for a maximum of 30 days. Staying longer means a Visitor's Permit Extension at an Immigration office — BZD 200 for each additional 30 days.
Most violent crime is concentrated in Belize City, especially the south side. Transit straight through to the water taxis or airport, avoid walking after dark, and use licensed taxis.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Belize?
faq.answer: Probably not: US, UK, EU, Canadian, Australian, New Zealand, CARICOM and most Commonwealth passports enter visa-free and are stamped in for up to 30 days. Nationalities that do need a visa apply at a Belizean consulate, or are generally exempted if they hold a valid multiple-entry US visa.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Belize?
faq.answer: The entry stamp is up to 30 days for everyone, including visa-free visitors. You can extend 30 days at a time at an Immigration office with a Visitor's Permit Extension, which costs BZD 200 (about USD 100) each time.

faq.question: Can I enter Belize with a US visa instead of a Belizean visa?
faq.answer: Generally yes — Belize waives its visa requirement for travelers holding a valid multiple-entry US visa. Carry the passport containing the visa and confirm current practice with the Belize Immigration Department before traveling, as admission always remains at the border officer's discretion.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Belize?
faq.answer: No. Belize's travel health insurance became optional in July 2022, when Statutory Instrument No. 100 of 2022 replaced the COVID-19 entry regulations and Cabinet removed all public-health measures at points of entry. Cover for medical emergencies is still sensible.

faq.question: Can I pay with US dollars in Belize?
faq.answer: Yes. The Belize dollar is pegged at exactly BZD 2 = USD 1 and US dollars are accepted almost everywhere. Just check which currency a quoted price is in — "dollars" can mean either.
